lessons.title: Dreams and what-ifs
lessons.goal: Talk about wishes and imagine hypothetical situations.

tip.title: Konjunktiv II
tip.body: For unreal situations use würde + infinitive, or the short forms wäre, hätte and könnte: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich mehr reisen. The verb goes to the end of the wenn-clause, and the main clause then starts with the verb. Pronunciation: hätte has a short ä like the e in "bed"; wäre has a long one, close to "air".

phrases.n: If I had more time, I would travel more.

lessons.title: Polite requests and advice
lessons.goal: Make polite requests and give a friend advice and suggestions.

tip.title: Softening with Konjunktiv II
tip.body: Könnten Sie and Würden Sie sound much more polite than Können Sie. For advice, use An deiner Stelle würde ich or Du solltest, and for suggestions Wie wäre es mit? Intonation tip: requests sound friendlier with a slight rise at the end and a warm, unhurried "bitte".

lessons.title: Dream job, dream home
lessons.goal: Describe the life you would like using Konjunktiv II and relative clauses.

tip.title: Relative clauses with a preposition
tip.body: A relative clause describes a noun and sends its verb to the end: ein Job, bei dem ich viel reisen kann. The preposition comes first and the pronoun matches the noun's gender and case: der Job → bei dem, die Wohnung → in der.

phrases.t: Ich hätte gern einen Job, bei dem ich viel reisen kann.
phrases.n: I'd like a job where I can travel a lot.
phrases.note: relative clause: verb at the end

lessons.title: Konjunktiv II forms
lessons.goal: Use wäre, hätte, könnte and würde with all persons.

tip.title: Short forms for sein, haben and modals
tip.body: Most verbs use würde + infinitive at the end: Ich würde reisen. But sein, haben and the modal verbs have their own forms with an umlaut: wäre, hätte, könnte, müsste. Endings work like the past tense: ich wäre, du wärst, wir wären.

lessons.title: A year anywhere
lessons.goal: Imagine and describe a different life for about 50 seconds.

culture.title: Was wäre, wenn das Volk entscheidet?
culture.body: In Switzerland, citizens vote on national questions several times a year — from taxes to motorway tolls. With 100,000 signatures, people can even propose a change to the constitution (Volksinitiative). Many Germans and Austrians discuss whether they would like more direct democracy too.
